You are a molecular design agent.
You may ONLY modify molecules using tools.
Only make one modification at a time.
Read the parameter descriptions for the tools very carefully.
Always ensure that your modifications don't break valence rules and do not result in a fragmented molecule.
After each successful tool call, check its result message and the updated atom table against what you intended - if it modified the wrong part of the molecule, call undo_last_change before continuing.
Every tool except crossover_molecules acts ONLY on your current working molecule (ligand 1) - none of them can see or touch the second candidate ligand. Treat ligand 2 as inspiration only: if you want to bring in one of its features, either call crossover_molecules to combine the two, or rebuild that feature yourself on your current working molecule (e.g. with add_substructure). An atom index you give to any tool other than crossover_molecules is always interpreted against your current working molecule, never against ligand 2 - do not reason about 'modifying ligand 2' and then call one of these tools, since the edit will land on the wrong molecule and likely do nothing you intended.

Both parents are active, so this is one case where their difference is informative rather than noise: ligand 2 reaches jnk3~0.10 but pays for it with QED 0.446 at 413 Da, while ligand 1 gets 0.08 at 319 Da with QED 0.672. Mass is clearly the wrong currency - the best Phi in the pool belongs to a 242 Da molecule. So I will upgrade the quality of the NH-azine link rather than add another ring system. Ligand 1 presents a plain pyrimidin-2-ylamino at atoms 15-21. I am replacing it with quinazolin-4-ylamino: the anilinoquinazoline is the archetypal ATP-competitive kinase recognition element, it keeps exactly the same single NH linker, and it is a fused electron-poor azine rather than a bare one. Atom 14 is the aromatic carbon carrying that nitrogen and the 14-15 bond is non-ring, so the swap is clean and costs only ~37 Da.

The quinazoline is in and SA is excellent at 1.85, but QED crashed to 0.477 - the fused benzo ring pushed LogP to 4.70 and the molecule to 369 Da with four aromatic rings. I have to pay for the quinazoline by deleting the benzyl urea arm, which is the part contributing nothing: atom 1 is the urea carbonyl and atom 2 is the NH joining it to the benzyl, a non-ring bond, so cutting there removes the NH, the CH2 and the whole phenyl in one modification. Putting a methyl on the carbonyl leaves N-{4-[(quinazolin-4-yl)amino]phenyl}acetamide at ~278 Da: three aromatic rings, 3 rotatable bonds, LogP back near 3.1, 2 donors. That keeps the anilinoquinazoline recognition element - the point of the probe - on a molecule small enough for QED to stay high.
